mainTopic: רבי's split ruling on stirring and covering a pot, the dispute about אפשר לסוחטו, and a new משנה on the udder and the heart
overview: This עמוד continues the case of a drop of milk that fell on one piece of meat cooking in a pot. רבי gave a split ruling: רבי יהודה seems right when one did not stir or cover from the start, and חכמים seem right when one stirred and covered. The גמרא first asks why רבי יהודה would forbid even with constant stirring. It answers that he worries the stirring was not thorough. Next it explains that the case where חכמים are right is stirring and covering from beginning to end. From this it infers that חכמים themselves permit even late stirring, so they must hold אפשר לסוחטו מותר. רב אחא מדפתי suggests the argument might really be about מין במינו. רבינא answers that only the אפשר לסוחטו reading explains why רבי gave one case to each side. Then a new משנה teaches that an udder and a heart should be torn open to remove their milk and blood, while the exact exemption and any remaining prohibition need the Gemara and commentaries to explain.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהודה forbid even with full stirring?
steps.stepSummary: From the way רבי limited רבי יהודה's view, the גמרא infers that רבי יהודה forbids even when the pot was stirred or covered the whole time. It then asks why, since the piece never absorbed the milk alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that רבי יהודה holds that even when one stirred from beginning to end and covered from beginning to end, it is forbidden. But why? The piece did not absorb the milk alone at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference about what רבי יהודה himself holds, and then attacks that inference as illogical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי accepted רבי יהודה only where one stirred late, so רבי יהודה himself must forbid even with stirring the whole time. But with constant stirring the milk spreads through the whole pot right away. The first piece never held the milk by itself, so the milk should be cancelled by the whole pot.

keyTerms.meaning: He stirred or shook the pot

phrases.english: By inference, Rabbi Yehuda holds:
when one stirred from beginning to end
and covered from beginning to end, it is forbidden.
Why? It did not absorb at all!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the first piece: it never soaked up the milk on its own, because the milk spread through the pot right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous עמוד's explanation of רבי's statement by drawing out what it implies about רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied position that רבי יהודה forbids even with stirring and covering the whole time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With constant stirring, the milk never sits in one piece, so there is no reason to judge by that piece alone

steps.title: רבי יהודה worries the stirring was not thorough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה is concerned that the stirring or covering was not done thoroughly enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: he did not stir really well, and he did not cover really well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה is strict even when someone stirred the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה fears that the stirring or covering was not complete. Then the milk may first have soaked into the one piece and made it forbidden, and that piece then forbids the rest. רבי does not share this worry, so he permits when one stirred properly.

phrases.english: Say: he did not stir thoroughly,
and he did not cover thoroughly.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind רבי יהודה's view: worry that the stirring was not complete
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Constant stirring means the milk could never have been absorbed by one piece alone
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה fears the stirring or covering was not thorough, so the first piece may have absorbed the milk first
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה is strict even with stirring the whole time, because he worries the stirring was not done thoroughly.

steps.title: What does 'stirred and covered' mean in רבי's statement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the second half of רבי's statement, about when חכמים are right, and asks what 'stirred and covered' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And the words of חכמים seem right when one stirred and covered.' What does 'stirred' mean, and what does 'covered' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of רבי's statement and asks for a definition. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has explained when רבי sides with רבי יהודה. Now it needs to know exactly which case of stirring and covering makes רבי side with חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי יהודה

phrases.english: The Master said: And the words of the Sages
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is רבי, whose statement in the ברייתא was quoted earlier.

phrases.english: apply when he stirred and covered.
What is 'stirred' and what is 'covered'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים כְּשֶׁנִּיעֵר וְכִסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי יהודה half of רבי's statement to the חכמים half
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of stirring and covering is meant in the statement that חכמים are right

steps.title: It cannot mean stirring only at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that 'stirred' means stirred only at the end. That case was already assigned to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means he stirred at the end and not at the beginning, and covered at the end and not at the beginning, didn't you already say that רבי יהודה's words seem right in that case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous עמוד, 'stirring only at the end' was the case where רבי sides with רבי יהודה. The same case cannot also be where רבי sides with חכמים. So this meaning is impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; if we suggest

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא נִיעֵר בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה,
phrases.english: If you say he stirred at the end and did not stir at the beginning,
and covered at the end and did not cover at the beginning,

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמְרַתְּ נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהָא!
phrases.english: didn't you say that the words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right in this case?
phrases.notes: This points back to the previous עמוד, where 'did not stir' was explained as stirring only at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא נִיעֵר בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects a first answer to the question in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that 'stirred and covered' means only at the end
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case was already identified as the one where רבי agrees with רבי יהודה

steps.title: It means stirring and covering the whole time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'stirred and covered' means he stirred and covered from beginning to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means he stirred from beginning to end and covered from beginning to end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct definition: stirring or covering the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since stirring only at the end is the רבי יהודה case, the חכמים case must be the stronger one: constant stirring or covering. In that case רבי says the whole pot cancels the milk.

keyTerms.meaning: From beginning to end; the whole time

phrases.english: Rather, he stirred from beginning to end,
and covered from beginning to end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after rejecting the first option in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Stirred and covered' means stirred and covered continuously from beginning to end
steps.whatToRemember: Stirring only at the end is where רבי sides with רבי יהודה. Stirring the whole time is where רבי sides with חכמים.

steps.title: Inference: חכמים permit even with stirring only at the end
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי agreed with חכמים only for constant stirring, the גמרא infers that חכמים themselves permit even when one stirred or covered only at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that רבנן hold that if he stirred at the end and not at the beginning, or covered at the end and not at the beginning, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference about what חכמים themselves hold. This sets up the next discussion, where that inference will be examined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי only partly accepted חכמים, limiting them to constant stirring. That suggests חכמים themselves go further and permit even late stirring. This means they hold that milk already absorbed by the first piece spreads back out through the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis; the Aramaic name for חכמים

phrases.english: By inference, the Rabbis hold:
if he stirred at the end and did not stir at the beginning,

phrases.aramaic: כִּסָּה בַּסּוֹף וְלֹא כִּסָּה בַּתְּחִלָּה – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: or covered at the end and did not cover at the beginning, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the implication of step 5 for the view of חכמים, just as step 1 did for רבי יהודה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חכמים themselves permit even when the stirring or covering came only at the end
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי, who is רבי יהודה הנשיא and makes the compromise statement, with רבי יהודה, who argues with חכמים in the ברייתא.

steps.title: So חכמים hold a squeezable piece is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its inference: חכמים must hold that אפשר לסוחטו מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that they hold that if it can be squeezed out, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the inference from Step 6 and states what חכמים must believe. Since they permit even when the stirring was only at the end, they must hold that a piece whose forbidden taste could be squeezed out is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that חכמים permit even late stirring or covering. That only makes sense if the first piece that absorbed the forbidden taste did not itself become a forbidden piece. So חכמים hold אפשר לסוחטו מותר, which means רבי יהודה (and רבי, in the case he agrees with him) hold it is forbidden. The two sides of the מחלוקת now line up with this question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to squeeze it out: the forbidden taste could, in theory, be pressed out of the piece

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading, the whole מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and חכמים is about אפשר לסוחטו: חכמים say permitted, רבי יהודה says forbidden.

phrases.english: Evidently, they hold
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: that something that can be squeezed out is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the legal principle behind the inference made in Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חכמים hold אפשר לסוחטו מותר, so the תנאים argue about this question.

steps.title: Maybe the argument is really about mixing with its own kind
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי suggests that everyone forbids a squeezable piece, and that רבי יהודה and חכמים argue only about מין במינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: How do you know they argue about whether a squeezable piece is permitted? Maybe everyone agrees it is forbidden, and they argue about a food mixed with its own kind. רבי יהודה follows his usual view that a food mixed with its own kind is not cancelled out, and חכמים follow their usual view that it is cancelled out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges רבינא's reading of the מחלוקת. He offers a different explanation that does not need the אפשר לסוחטו principle at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said the argument proves that תנאים disagree about אפשר לסוחטו. רב אחא points out that both sides could be explained by a different, well-known מחלוקת: whether מין במינו can be בטל. If that works, there is no proof that anyone holds אפשר לסוחטו מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: A food mixed with the same kind of food
Is cancelled out (nullified) in the mixture

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He is only saying that the ברייתא does not prove that anyone permits a squeezable piece, because there is another way to explain it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
From where do you know that they argue about something that can be squeezed out?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Perhaps everyone agrees that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden,
and here they argue about a kind mixed with its own kind,
and Rabbi Yehuda follows his reasoning, for he said:
a kind mixed with its own kind is not cancelled out,
and the Rabbis follow their reasoning, for they say:
a kind mixed with its own kind is cancelled out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 7 by offering a different basis for the מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the ברייתא shows a תנאים dispute about אפשר לסוחטו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another explanation fits: the sides could be arguing about מין במינו, with everyone forbidding a squeezable piece.

steps.title: רבי's split view fits the squeezing explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that only if the argument is about אפשר לסוחטו does it make sense for רבי to agree with רבי יהודה in one case and with חכמים in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of argument is this? It works well if you say that here חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about a food mixed with its own kind, and they argue about something that can be squeezed out. That explains why רבי said: The words of רבי יהודה seem right in this case, and the words of חכמים seem right in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב אחא's idea. He starts with the first half of his proof: his own reading explains רבי's wording well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is about אפשר לסוחטו, then the timing of the stirring really matters, so it makes sense that רבי sides with each opinion in a different case. In this reading, חכמים here agree that מין במינו is not בטל, so that is not the point of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a way of saying the objection does not hold up)
It works well if... (the first half of a comparison)

phrases.english: What is this?
phrases.notes: This is רבינא answering רב אחא.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that the Rabbis, regarding a kind with its own kind,
hold like Rabbi Yehuda here,
and they argue about something that can be squeezed out —
that is why Rebbi said:
The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right in this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is when he did not stir or cover from the start.

phrases.english: and the words of the Sages in that case.
phrases.notes: "That case" is when he stirred and covered from beginning to end (Step 5).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge from Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of רבי's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא could be read as a מין במינו dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the אפשר לסוחטו reading explains why רבי gave each side a case.

steps.title: The own-kind explanation does not fit רבי's wording
steps.stepSummary: If the argument were only about מין במינו, רבי should have said 'רבי יהודה seems right, and does not seem right,' and that would be all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that everyone forbids something that can be squeezed out, and here they argue about a food mixed with its own kind, then רבי should have said: 'The words of רבי יהודה seem right, and do not seem right,' and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his answer by showing that רב אחא's reading does not fit רבי's words. This closes the back-and-forth in favor of the אפשר לסוחטו reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב אחא's reading, רבי would simply agree with רבי יהודה that מין במינו is not בטל. He would only disagree with רבי יהודה's worry that the stirring was not thorough. So he should have said 'רבי יהודה is right in one case and not right in the other,' and there would be no reason to bring in the words of חכמים at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say (the second half of the comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's wording, which gives one case to רבי יהודה and one to חכמים, proves that the argument is about אפשר לסוחטו and not about מין במינו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבינא's claim that תנאים disagree about whether a piece whose forbidden taste could be squeezed out is permitted.

phrases.english: But if you say:
everyone agrees that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden,
and here they argue about a kind with its own kind —
then this: 'The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right
and do not seem right' is what he should have said,
phrases.notes: Right when he did not stir at the start, and not right when he stirred from the start.

phrases.english: and nothing more.
phrases.notes: He would have no reason to mention the words of חכמים at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא comparison that began in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אחא's suggestion that the dispute is only about מין במינו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It cannot explain why רבי sided with חכמים in a case, instead of just accepting and rejecting רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The udder: tear it and remove its milk
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the כְּחָל (udder) should be torn and its milk taken out before cooking. If one did not tear it, he does not violate the prohibition of בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The udder: one tears it and takes out its milk. If he did not tear it, he does not violate the prohibition because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It tells us how to prepare an udder for cooking, and what happens if that step was skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An udder is meat that has milk trapped inside it, so the משנה says to tear it open and remove the milk first. But if one cooked it without tearing, he has not broken the Torah law of בשר בחלב. This shows that milk still inside the udder does not count as real 'milk' for that Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
He does not transgress the prohibition because of it

steps.confusionAlert: Here חֶלְבּוֹ means 'its milk' (from חָלָב). It does NOT mean forbidden fat (חֵלֶב). The whole topic is meat and milk.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion about whether skipping the tearing is fully allowed, or only free of a Torah violation.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַכְּחָל – קוֹרְעוֹ וּמוֹצִיא אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ.
phrases.english: MISHNA: The udder: one tears it open and takes out its milk.
If he did not tear it, he does not violate a prohibition because of it.
phrases.notes: He means he hasn't broken the Torah law of meat and milk. The משנה still wants him to tear it from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַכְּחָל – קוֹרְעוֹ וּמוֹצִיא אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The sugya about אפשר לסוחטו has ended. A new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before cooking an udder, one should tear it and remove its milk. If he did not, he has not violated the Torah prohibition of בשר בחלב.

steps.title: The heart: tear it and remove its blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says to tear the heart and remove its blood. The statement that one does not transgress is explained as exemption from the specified punishment in the relevant case, not blanket permission to eat the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heart: one tears it and takes out its blood. If he did not tear it, he does not violate the prohibition because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second ruling that matches the first one. This time it is about the heart and the blood inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rashi explains the Mishnah as a bird heart whose blood is less than a כזית, so there is no כרת for that amount. The continuation still calls a half-measure of blood forbidden by Torah law. Tosafos disputes Rashi about cooked blood and distinguishes raw from cooked cases. Do not read אינו עובר עליו as saying that every untorn heart may be eaten without a Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating דם. Here he is not liable for it.

steps.whatToRemember: Tear the udder or heart first. The words אינו עובר עליו do not by themselves mean that eating it is permitted; the heart case still has an eating prohibition.

phrases.english: The heart: one tears it open and takes out its blood.
If he did not tear it, he does not violate a prohibition because of it.
phrases.notes: Here the prohibition is eating blood, not meat and milk like the udder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a parallel second clause of the same משנה, applying the udder's pattern to the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tear the heart and remove its blood. אינו עובר עליו limits punishment in the case explained by the commentaries; it does not give blanket permission to eat the blood.
